Danish Police fitness admission test

POLICE ENTRY TEST

At a glance

Danish Police uses a six-part fitness test for admission. The test includes a 2,400 m run. The running time and other targets depend on the published criteria.

FEATURED ACTIVITY2,400 m runMen 12:00 · women 13:30 maximum

What the test includes

  • Warm-up routine
  • Speed test
  • Standing long jump
  • Pull-ups
  • Bench press
  • 2,400 m run

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

Six mandatory parts in a roughly three-hour assessment including feedback. The prescribed warm-up is itself a test and lasts approximately 15 minutes.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

EventMenWomen
Prescribed warm-upComplete programmeComplete programme
Figure-eight speed test17.5 s or faster18.7 s or faster
Standing long jump210 cm160 cm
Approved body pulls45
Bench press10 reps at 50 kg10 reps at 30 kg
2,400 m run12:00 or faster13:30 or faster

Scoring and scope

All six parts must be passed. Speed course uses two cones 13.4 m apart and 2¼ circuits; jump results round down to 5 cm. The published body-pull instructions differ by category: use the official demonstration rather than assuming identical pull-ups. Bench load includes the bar. Body pulls and bench each allow two attempts.

  • Men: official instructions
  • Women: official instructions

Before you rehearse the test

  1. Use the official demonstration for each body-pull variation and mark the speed course exactly as shown by the publisher.
  2. Practise the complete prescribed warm-up before the other components, rather than testing every event fresh on unrelated days.

Warm-up and speed course

The prescribed warm-up lasts 15 minutes. For the figure-eight speed course, the cones are 13.4 m apart and the route covers two and a quarter circuits. Use the official diagram for the start, finish and turning direction; the men’s and women’s time thresholds differ.

Standing long jump

Use the official two-attempt procedure. Distance is rounded down to the nearest 5 cm. The published minimums are 210 cm for men and 160 cm for women.

Body pulls and bench press

The body-pull movement differs between the men’s and women’s protocols: use the official demonstrations. Bench press is ten repetitions at the stated total weight, including the bar. Use a spotter or appropriate safety equipment for independent practice.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Practise the prescribed warm-up as a sequence, then learn the figure-eight course at low speed before adding timed efforts.
  • Use controlled bench press with a spotter or safeties. Train the appropriate body-pull variant and standing jump separately.
  • On a measured 400 m track, 12:00 over 2,400 m corresponds to six 2:00 laps; 13:30 corresponds to six 2:15 laps. Build pacing with easy running and shorter intervals.

Putting it into a training week

Practise warm-up, figure-eight turns and running splits on separate days before rehearsing the whole battery. Leave recovery between demanding sessions.

Common mistakes

  • Treating the warm-up as optional; using the wrong body-pull technique or excluding the bar from bench weight.
  • Testing a fresh 2,400 m run but never practising the sequence at a controlled effort.

What to log

Record applicant category, approved reps and total bar weight, jump distance, course time and six lap splits.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

Worth knowing

  • Applicants need to pass all six parts of the test.
  • Danish Police publishes separate guidance for men and women; use the page that applies to you.
